'''Rubén Oscar Wolkowyski''' (born September 30, 1973) is an Argentine former professional [[basketball]] player, who also holds Polish citizenship.<ref name="Euroleague.net Player Profile">[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?seasoncode=E2007&pcode=BCE Euroleague.net Player Profile]</ref>  At a height of {{convert|2.08|m|abbr=on}} tall, he played at the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[center (basketball)|center]] positions.<ref>[http://www.latinbasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=ARG&PlayerID=7173 Ruben Wolkowyski]. Latin-Basket</ref>

==Professional career==
Wolkowyski played professionally in Argentina, the United States, Russia, Poland, Spain, and Greece. In [[2000–01 NBA season|2000]], he and [[Pepe Sánchez (basketball)|Pepe Sánchez]] became the first Argentines to play in the [[NBA]] regular season. Wolkowyski played a total of 41 NBA games and averaged 2 points and 1.1 rebounds per game. His final game being on Christmas of 2002 in an 81 - 117 loss to the New Jersey Nets where he recorded 1 assist, 1 turnover and no other stats in 6 and half minutes of playing time.

On September 29, 2010, Wolkowyski scored 45 points for [[Libertad de Sunchales]] in a 118–115 victory over [[Obras Sanitarias]], for the [[Copa Argentina de Básquetbol|Copa Argentina]] title.<ref name=CL>{{cite news|url=http://www.canchallena.com/1309440-un-partido-para-la-historia |title=Un partido para la historia |newspaper=[[La Nación|Cancha Llena]] |language=es |date=2010-09-29 |access-date=2010-09-29 }}</ref> The winner of the game was decided after 4 over-times.<ref name=CL/>

==National team career==
Wolkowyski defended [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]] to claim the inaugural gold medal at the [[Basketball at the 1995 Pan American Games|1995 Pan American Games]] in the defeat in the final of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]], in [[Mar del Plata, Argentina]]. 
He defended Argentina in the win at the [[2001 Tournament of the Americas]], and at the [[2003 Tournament of the Americas|2003]] [[FIBA Americas Championship]]s, the [[2002 FIBA World Championship|2002]] and [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]s, and for the gold medal at the [[Basketball at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|1996]] and [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympics]].

==Personal life==
He played in Russia as a [[Europe]]an player, rather than as an Argentine, after Wolkowyski obtained Polish citizenship through his [[Warsaw]]-born grandfather, Anatol, who left Poland before World War II, to Argentina via Paraguay. His family spoke [[Polish language|Polish]] at home, but he does not know the language and communicates only in [[Spanish language|Spanish]] and [[English language|English]].<ref>[http://www.se.pl/archiwum/chce-sie-nauczyc-polskiego_36524.html Chcę się nauczyć polskiego] {{in lang|pl}}</ref><ref>[http://miasta.gazeta.pl/trojmiasto/1,35617,4438096.html Rozmowa z Rubenem Wołkowyskim] {{in lang|pl}}</ref>
